title: min-content, max-content, fit-content
learningObjectives: Explain min-content, max-content, fit-content and use selectors or sizing rules appropriately.

understand.concept: min-content is the smallest size a box can take without avoidable overflow, often based on its longest unbreakable segment. max-content is the preferred size without soft wrapping. fit-content() clamps a size between intrinsic limits and the available space using its supplied limit.
understand.whyItMatters: These values explain why content can expand a layout or wrap unexpectedly. Use them with grid and width constraints to create layouts that respect content without forcing overflow.
understand.analogy: min-content is the tightest content-driven fit, max-content is the unwrapped preference, and fit-content balances the preference against a limit.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; selector matching and sizing follow CSS specifications and browser layout algorithms.
